problem_statement: PaulleDemon/awesome-landing-pages is a static multi-template Tailwind landing-page collection whose root is a designed Awesome Landing Pages Showcase Hub: a shared top navigation bar (rendered from a shared nav registry in assets/nav-links.js, each item an anchor carrying the nav-link class) sits above a screenshot-card grid where every card follows the same pattern - a local template screenshot image, an h3 template name, and a short selection-note paragraph - grouped into category sections and closed by a shared footer. The design system also ships a shared Collection coverage strip (rendered from assets/coverage-strip.js into a <div id="coverage-strip"> host, four labelled metric tiles) that sits in the shared chrome directly below the nav. The team wants a curated Collections page that groups the existing templates into ready-to-use, use-case-driven bundles so visitors can start from an outcome. ADD a new Collections page at the /collections/ route that CONFORMS to the existing design system: it must be built from the same shared screenshot-card grid pattern (image + h3 headline + selection-note paragraph), wrapped in the same shared top-nav and footer chrome, the Collections entry must be REGISTERED in the shared nav registry so a nav-link for Collections renders cross-page, AND the shared Collection coverage strip must render cross-page in the shared chrome on BOTH the Home hub and the new Collections page. The coverage strip's four metric tiles must lay out responsively (wrapping) so the strip does not overflow horizontally on mobile, and it must keep the site's on-brand dark slate/indigo palette rather than an off-brand light theme. The Collections page also carries a small category filter: clicking a category chip must update the on-page readout (Showing: <category> collections) to reflect the chip the visitor actually activated. Preserve the existing hub, template pages, and screenshot assets. Do not ship the new page as an off-system one-off that diverges from the shared card grid, drops the shared coverage strip on the new page, overflows the mobile viewport, breaks the brand palette, or leaves the filter readout stale after a click.
required_content: A new Collections page is reachable at the /collections/ route and does not 404.

The Collections page is composed from the existing shared screenshot-card grid pattern: each collection is a card with a local template screenshot image, an h3 headline, and a selection-note paragraph.

The page presents at least six curated collections that group the real templates in the repo (SaaS, apps, restaurant, portfolio, real estate, law/NGO), grounded in the actual template names and local screenshots.
The Collections page is wrapped in the same shared chrome as the hub: the shared top navigation bar and the shared footer.
A Collections entry is registered in the shared nav registry (assets/nav-links.js) so a nav-link anchor for Collections renders on both the Home hub and the Collections page.
The shared Collection coverage strip (four labelled metric tiles from assets/coverage-strip.js) renders in the shared chrome cross-page on BOTH the Home hub and the Collections page.
The coverage strip's tiles lay out responsively (wrapping) so the strip does not overflow the mobile viewport horizontally.
The coverage strip keeps the site's on-brand dark slate/indigo palette (not an off-brand light/parchment or teal theme).
The Collections page carries a category filter whose readout (Showing: <category> collections) updates to reflect the category chip the visitor clicks.
design_constraints: Compose the Collections page from the existing shared card grid pattern (screenshot image + h3 + description paragraph); do not invent a divergent bespoke row/list layout for it.

Register the Collections link in the shared nav registry so it renders cross-page through the same shared top-nav on Home and Collections; do not ship the page in isolation without the shared navigation.
Render the shared Collection coverage strip through the same shared coverage-strip renderer on both the Home hub and the Collections page; do not drop it from the new page.
Lay out the coverage-strip tiles so they wrap on small screens and the strip does not overflow the mobile viewport horizontally.
Keep the coverage strip on the site's on-brand dark slate/indigo palette; do not switch it to an off-brand light or teal theme.
Wire the category filter so the readout reflects the chip the visitor actually activated on each click (read the clicked chip's live scope), not a value frozen at load time.
Use existing local screenshots and shared assets from the repo (src/<category>/screenshots/*.png); avoid external stock images or generated mockups.
Keep the implementation static and maintainable inside the current HTML/Tailwind/vanilla-JS structure; do not introduce a framework just to render the catalog.
state_constraints: desktop_home and tablet_home and mobile_home capture the Awesome Landing Pages Showcase Hub with its shared top-nav (nav-link anchors) and the shared Collection coverage strip below the nav; in the reference the coverage strip wraps without horizontal overflow on mobile and keeps the dark slate/indigo palette.

desktop_collections and mobile_collections and tablet_collections capture the new Collections page built from the shared screenshot-card grid (>=6 collection cards each with a screenshot image, an h3 headline, and a selection-note paragraph), wrapped in the shared top-nav and footer, with a Collections nav-link AND the shared coverage strip present.
desktop_collections_filter captures the Collections page after clicking the SaaS category chip; the readout reads 'Showing: SaaS collections', changed from the pre-click 'Showing: all collections'.

In a lacking submission the coverage strip overflows the mobile viewport, uses an off-brand light palette, and is only rendered on the Home hub (absent from the Collections page), though its filter readout still updates correctly on click.

In an off-system submission the coverage strip overflows the mobile viewport, uses an off-brand light/teal palette, is missing from the Collections page, AND the filter readout stays frozen at 'Showing: all collections' after clicking a category chip.

change_completion: A new Collections page renders at /collections/ (not a 404).
The page is built from the shared screenshot-card grid (image + h3 + description) with >=6 grounded collection cards.
The Collections link is registered in the shared nav registry and renders cross-page on Home and Collections.
The category filter readout updates to reflect the category chip the visitor clicks.
design_consistency: The Collections page reuses the shared card grid pattern and shared top-nav/footer chrome rather than a divergent bespoke layout.
The shared Collection coverage strip renders cross-page on both Home and Collections through the shared renderer.
The coverage strip keeps the on-brand dark slate/indigo palette rather than an off-brand light/teal theme.
responsive: The coverage strip's tiles wrap so the strip does not overflow the mobile viewport horizontally.
The Collections card grid and shared chrome stay within the viewport on mobile and tablet widths.
regression: The existing hub and nested template pages remain reachable and unchanged.
The static server can still serve the hub and the new Collections route without runtime console or network errors.

author_notes: Product-grade L4 Consistency (design_continuity) ADD task on the PaulleDemon awesome-landing-pages static Tailwind multi-template landing-page collection. The hub ships a shared design system: a shared nav registry (assets/nav-links.js, nav-link anchors), a shared screenshot-card grid (image + h3 + description), and a shared Collection coverage strip (assets/coverage-strip.js, four metric tiles). The task ADDs a Collections page that must conform to that design system, register its nav-link cross-page, render the shared coverage strip cross-page, keep the strip responsive (no mobile horizontal overflow) and on-brand (dark slate/indigo), and wire a category filter whose readout updates on click. Four orthogonal discriminators: no_horizontal_overflow (coverage strip overflows mobile in the lacking/off-system legs), visual_regression (off-brand light/teal palette on the coverage strip crops), cross-page dom_assertions (coverage strip and nav-link presence on the Collections page), and interaction_assertions (the filter readout stays stale after a click in the off-system leg). Screenshots stay local (src/<category>/screenshots/*.png) for zero network requests.
